– the failing test (signature + snippet),

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

Title: Diagnosis  
Details: The test `shouldReadBigGid()` sets a very large group ID (4294967294L) on a TarArchiveEntry, uses a TarArchiveOutputStream with POSIX big number mode, writes it out, and then reads it back with TarArchiveInputStream. The bug report details that reading entries with a UID or GID >= 0x80000000 (2147483648) causes a NumberFormatException. In the TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry() method, the actual TarArchiveEntry is created from raw header bytes by calling the constructor which calls parseTarHeader().  

Looking into TarArchiveEntry.parseTarHeader(), the UID and GID fields are parsed by calling TarUtils.parseOctalOrBinary(). This method detects if the field is in octal or binary format. If the highest bit is set (indicating binary), then for fields shorter than 9 bytes, it calls parseBinaryLong(), otherwise parseBinaryBigInteger(). For large UID or GID values (like 4294967294L which is 0xFFFFFFFE), the field length is likely less than 9 bytes, so parseBinaryLong() is called.  

parseBinaryLong() expects a maximum length of 8 bytes, treats the bytes as a signed long, and handles negative values via two's complement. But the UID/GID is an unsigned 32-bit value, and casting to int in parseTarHeader() truncates large values to negative due to overflow. The cast to int at lines 998 and 1000 in parseTarHeader() causes the values >= 0x80000000 to wrap into negative numbers or cause parsing to fail, because Java ints are signed 32-bit and the parsing logic is designed for signed values. POSIX headers do not define exact widths or signedness for these headers, leading to ambiguity.  

Hence, the bug arises because UID/GID fields are parsed as signed ints and limited by signed 32-bit integer range, but the test and the reported archive include larger unsigned values. This causes exceptions on reading large UID or GID values >= 0x80000000. The root cause is the parsing and storing of uid/gid fields as signed int instead of a wider or unsigned type, and possibly improper handling in parseBinaryLong for unsigned 32-bit big values.  

Recent reports do not provide additional clues. The root cause is evident from the current report and code inspection: the intermediate representation using int type for UID/GID and the method parseBinaryLong limits field length and interprets values as signed leading to failure when encountering large unsigned values as produced by some systems (macOS 'nobody' uid 429496729).

Recommended fix involves changing the types used to store UID/GID in TarArchiveEntry (should support long or unsigned types) and adjusting parsing to correctly interpret large unsigned values in POSIX format extended headers.

Which methods to fix:
- TarArchiveEntry.parseTarHeader(byte[], ZipEncoding, boolean)
- TarUtils.parseOctalOrBinary(byte[], int, int)
- TarUtils.parseBinaryLong(byte[], int, int, boolean)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveEntry.parseTarHeader(byte[], org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipEncoding, boolean)
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarUtils.parseOctalOrBinary(byte[], int, int)
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarUtils.parseBinaryLong(byte[], int, int, boolean)
